record.paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
record.original_question: Is the class of languages generated by conjunctive grammars closed under complementation? Equivalently, for every conjunctive grammar G over a fixed alphabet, is the complement of the language L(G) also generated by some conjunctive grammar?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A conjunctive grammar over a finite alphabet Σ is a tuple G = (Σ, N, R, S), where N is a finite set of nonterminals, S ∈ N is the start symbol, and R is a finite set of rules of the form A → α₁ & α₂ & ⋯ & αₘ with m ≥ 1 and each αᵢ ∈ (Σ ∪ N)*. The semantics is given by the least fixed point of language equations: each nonterminal A is interpreted as a language L(A) ⊆ Σ*, where for every rule A → α₁ & ⋯ & αₘ in R, L(α₁) ∩ ⋯ ∩ L(αₘ) ⊆ L(A), with concatenation of languages extended to strings of terminals and nonterminals in the usual way. The language generated by G is L(G) = L(S). Let 𝓛_conj denote the class of all languages of the form L(G) for some conjunctive grammar G.

Question: Is 𝓛_conj closed under complementation? Equivalently, for every conjunctive grammar G over an alphabet Σ, does there exist a conjunctive grammar G' over Σ such that L(G') = Σ* ∖ L(G)?
artifact.status_search_result: The complement closure problem for the class of conjunctive languages appears to remain open. Closure under complement is known for the linear subfamily (linear conjunctive grammars, e.g. via trellis automata), but no resolution of the question for general conjunctive grammars is found in the literature; recent surveys and overviews continue to list it as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the closure properties of linear conjunctive languages
status_evidence.snippet: Linear conjunctive languages are closed under complement, hence under all Boolean operations.
status_evidence.claim: Only the linear subclass is known to be closed under complement; the general case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: A Tale of Conjunctive Grammars
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of conjunctive grammar results and open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of conjunctive grammars continue to list complement closure as open.

status_evidence.title: Conjunctive grammar - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Closure under complement and under ε-free homomorphism are open problems for conjunctive grammars.
status_evidence.claim: Wikipedia explicitly identifies complementation closure for conjunctive grammars as an open problem.
